title: Agent Collectives Should Not Detect Their Own Imposters: A Chess Case Study
abstract: arXiv:2605.09027v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Collectives of AI agents can outperform any single agent on complex tasks, yet remain vulnerable to imposters that deliberately mislead their peers. Because even one such imposter can sabotage the collective, reliable detection is essential. We examine two strategies: embedding detection inside the participating agents, or employing a dedicated external detector that observes the deliberation without joining it. On a deliberately small but challenging chess-based testbed, we find that simply warning agents of possible imposters is counterproductive. It degrades decisions even in the absence of adversaries, triggers unhelpful social dynamics, and leaks information to the imposter. An external detector avoids these pitfalls, yet must continually adapt as imposters evolve new strategies. We show that a lightweight meta-trained detector can rapidly recalibrate to unseen attacks from only a handful of examples, far more efficiently

translated_title: 智能体集体不应自行检测其内部的冒名顶替者：一个国际象棋案例研究
translated_abstract: AI智能体集体在复杂任务上可以超越任何单一智能体，但仍然容易受到故意误导同伴的冒名顶替者（imposter）的攻击。由于哪怕只有一个冒名顶替者也可能破坏整个集体，可靠的检测机制至关重要。我们研究了两种策略：将检测功能嵌入参与智能体自身内部，或者雇佣一个专门的、只观察但不参与集体讨论的外部检测器。在一个特意设计的小型但具有挑战性的国际象棋测试平台上，我们发现仅仅警告智能体可能存在冒名顶替者反而会产生反效果：即使在没有对手的情况下，它也会降低决策质量，引发无益的社交动态，并向冒名顶替者泄露信息。外部检测器虽然可以避免这些陷阱，但必须随着冒名顶替者演化出新策略而不断适应。我们证明，一个轻量级的元训练检测器仅凭少量样本就能快速重新校准，以应对未见过的攻击，其效率远高于其他方法。
tldr: 研究表明让智能体集体自行检测内部冒名顶替者会适得其反，而采用能够从少量样本快速适应新型攻击的轻量级元训练外部检测器才是更优策略。
en_tdlr: Embedding imposter detection within agent collectives is counterproductive; instead, a lightweight meta-trained external detector can rapidly recalibrate to unseen attacks using only a handful of examples.
